# std.result

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Result helpers.

## Functions

### `and_then`

```badger
fn and_then<T, U, E>(r: Result<T, E>, f: once fn(T) -> Result<U, E>) -> Result<U, E>
```

Chain a fallible step: `f` runs only on success.

### `bail`

```badger
fn bail<T, E>(error: E) -> Result<T, E>
```

Leave the current function with `error`: `return result.bail(error)`.
The result's value type is the one the caller expects, so a guard
clause reads as one line:

```badger
if title == "" { return bail(AppError.invalid_input("title required")) }
```

### `bimap`

```badger
fn bimap<T, U, E, F>(r: Result<T, E>, ok_fn: fn(T) -> U, err_fn: fn(E) -> F) -> Result<U, F>
```

Map both sides of a result: `ok_fn` on success, `err_fn` on failure.
The counterpart of `map` and `map_err` for the common "change the
error type on the way out" case.

### `check`

```badger
fn check<T, E>(value: T, valid: fn(&T) -> Bool, error: fn() -> E) -> Result<T, E>
```

The value when `valid` accepts it, `err(error())` otherwise. The error
is built only when the value is rejected.

### `error`

```badger
fn error<T, E>(r: Result<T, E>) -> Option<E>
```

The error, if failed.

### `flatten`

```badger
fn flatten<T, E>(r: Result<Result<T, E>, E>) -> Result<T, E>
```

Remove one level of nesting.

### `is_ok`

```badger
fn is_ok<T, E>(r: Result<T, E>) -> Bool
```

### `map`

```badger
fn map<T, U, E>(r: Result<T, E>, f: fn(T) -> U) -> Result<U, E>
```

### `map_err`

```badger
fn map_err<T, E, F>(r: Result<T, E>, f: fn(E) -> F) -> Result<T, F>
```

### `must`

```badger
fn must<E>(condition: Bool, error: E) -> Result<Unit, E>
```

`ok(())` when `condition` holds, `err(error)` otherwise. The result can
be chained with `?` or returned directly.

### `must_eq`

```badger
fn must_eq<T, E>(a: T, b: T, error: E) -> Result<Unit, E> where T: Eq
```

`ok(())` when `a` and `b` are equal, `err(error)` otherwise.

### `or_else`

```badger
fn or_else<T, E, F>(r: Result<T, E>, f: once fn(E) -> Result<T, F>) -> Result<T, F>
```

Recover from a failure: `f` runs only on an error and may fail with
another error type.

### `transpose`

```badger
fn transpose<T, E>(r: Result<Option<T>, E>) -> Option<Result<T, E>>
```

`Result<Option<T>, E>` as `Option<Result<T, E>>`: `ok(none)` is absent.

### `unwrap_or`

```badger
fn unwrap_or<T, E>(r: Result<T, E>, default: T) -> T
```

### `unwrap_or_else`

```badger
fn unwrap_or_else<T, E>(r: Result<T, E>, fallback: once fn(E) -> T) -> T
```

The value, or `fallback(error)` computed only on failure.

### `value`

```badger
fn value<T, E>(r: Result<T, E>) -> Option<T>
```

The value, if successful.
